entities.summary:
Illig Qaghan, born Ashina Duobi, posthumous name Prince Huang of Guiyi (歸義荒王), was the last qaghan of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate.

He ruled from approximately 628 to 634 CE, during a period of significant instability in the region.

The collapse of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate led to the fragmentation of the region into smaller khanates and the eventual Mongol conquest of the area.

Illig Qaghan's legacy is marked by the continued influence of Turkic culture in the region, particularly in the art and architecture of the Mongols.

In the annals of history, Illig Qaghan's reign serves as a testament to the resilience of the Turkic people in the face of external pressures.

Like a fading ember, the memory of Illig Qaghan's rule burns bright, a beacon of hope in a world forever changed by the tides of history.

As the last qaghan of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, Illig Qaghan's story is one of survival, adaptation, and the unyielding spirit of a people who refused to be extinguished by the flames of time.
